campaigns.title: This Pitru Paksha, help feed warm meals to abandoned elderly and the destitute
campaigns.description: For thousands of elderly people, homeless individuals, daily-wage workers and vulnerable families, hunger is not an occasional hardship, it is a daily reality. Danirasa Foundation’s with the help of kind supporters and donors is quietly changing this reality for hundreds each day. Your donation provides a warm meal to an elderly grandparent who has no other means to survive. Donate Now.Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).From one crisis to a mission against hungerDanirasa Foundation’s journey began during the devastating 2015 Chennai floods. Founder Indu Priya witnessed families, especially women and children, struggling with displacement and hunger. She and her team mobilised volunteers to cook and distribute hot meals. What began as an emergency response became a lasting commitment to ensuring vulnerable communities have access to food with dignity and care.Today, Danirasa’s Community Kitchen serves around 4,900 people through this programme. The meals reach elderly residents in old-age homes, children from underserved communities, rehabilitation centres, homeless people, daily-wage workers and others facing food insecurity.A meal can mean so much moreFor an elderly person living without family support, a nutritious meal can bring comfort. For someone surviving on irregular daily wages, it can mean one less worry. For a vulnerable child, it can provide the nourishment needed to learn and grow.But feeding thousands of people every day requires a steady supply of ingredients, cooking, packaging, transportation and dedicated people.Help serve a meal with dignityYour donation can help Danirasa continue providing nutritious meals to homeless and elderly people, children, workers, persons with disabilities and families struggling to make ends meet.Help Danirasa ensure that no vulnerable person has to face the day with an empty stomach. Donate today.Donate to this fundraiser by give.do, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Danirasa Foundation, in its mission to feed helpless elderly and destitute people, who have no means of survival.

campaigns.title: This Pitru Paksha, be a saviour of an abandoned elderly person left to die alone
campaigns.description: For elderly people left alone in the final chapters of their lives, abandonment can mean a life of suffering on the streets. A life filled with loneliness, insecurity and fear. Our NGO partner Neptune Foundation has been a pillar of support for countless such abandoned grandparents, neglected and destitute senior citizens, helping them find something that many thought they had lost forever, a safe place to call homeThe NGO sustains its old age home through public support and is in urgent needs for donations and funds to keep the shelter going. Your donation can go a long way in giving these elderly parents the home they deserve. Donate generously!Donate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking.Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).A home when there is nowhere else to goNeptune Foundation provides free shelter, nutritious food, healthcare, companionship and emotional support to elderly people who have been abandoned, rejected or left without the means to care for themselves. Many residents are widowed, living alone, economically vulnerable, medically fragile or have experienced neglect and abuse.Today, 41 senior citizens between the ages of 60 and 95 live at the home. They receive hygienically prepared meals, regular medical check-ups, nursing and caregiving support, recreational and spiritual activities, and a safe residential environment. Here, an elderly person is not treated as a burden. Festivals, birthdays and cultural activities bring residents together, creating companionship and a sense of togetherness and belonging. The home welcomes seniors without discrimination based on caste, religion or background.Donate to give them a life filled with dignityThe need is growing. Neptune Foundation plans to expand its facility from 41 residents to up to 200 elderly people and establish a primary health centre serving residents as well as nearby rural communities.Your donation can help provide free food, shelter, medical care and daily support to elderly grandparents who have nowhere else to turn.Help Neptune Foundation give abandoned seniors more than a roof, a loving home, dignity, companionship and care. Donate today.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Neptune Foundation, in its mission to care for abandoned elderly grandparents.

campaigns.title: Help visually impaired Shivaprakash give 40 blind girls shelter, education and care
campaigns.description: At the age of 8, Shivaprakash lost his vision. But what could have become a life of despair became something else entirely. Shivaprakash went on to complete his Master’s degree and eventually founded the Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust, an organisation born out of personal struggle and driven by a powerful mission, to educate and empower blind girls, who are among the most neglected and marginalised in society.In many families, blind daughters are hidden away, seen as a burden, and in some cases, even as a curse. They are denied the right to dream, grow, or be independent. At Divya Jyothi, Shivaprakash is changing that narrative. Your support can ensure that no blind girl is left behind simply because of her disability. Donate today to help them stand tall, proud, and self-reliant. Donate nowDonate easily through UPI, all debit/credit cards and net banking. Charitable donations to this fundraising campaign are tax exempted under 80G of the Income Tax Act (India).Education is survivalIn communities where gender and disability intersect, blind girls face deep-rooted prejudice and extreme isolation. Many are denied even basic schooling and are left dependent on family members for the rest of their lives. Recognising this, Divya Jyothi began with a simple yet radical step: to provide blind girls with computer training so they could access the digital world and open doors to employment.But the journey didn’t stop there. The NGO went on to launch a braille transcription centre, ensuring girls have access to learning materials that suit their needs. As Shivaprakash says, “Without education, no one can do anything. That's why education is even more important for blind girls.” Education isn’t just about literacy, it’s about self-worth, decision-making, mobility, and freedom. It’s about giving these girls the same right to participate in society that sighted individuals often take for granted.From rejection to respectIn a country where blind girls are often treated as liabilities, Divya Jyothi is rewriting their futures. Over 1,000 girls have graduated from the Trust’s training centres. Many of them come from families that had almost given up on them. Today, these same girls are government employees, corporate professionals, and role models in their communities.More than 200 graduates have secured jobs in the public sector. Over 300 are now employed in private companies. Every success story is proof that with the right support, blind girls don’t just survive, they thrive. “Most girls are neglected by their families. This is a major challenge for them,” says Shivaprakash. By providing them with skills and confidence, Divya Jyothi is turning neglect into empowerment and helplessness into hope.Donate to help 40 blind girls find independenceAlmost 40 girls are currently enrolled and will directly benefit from your support. These are girls with potential, courage, and ambition—but they lack the resources to pursue an independent life. “I request each one to come forward and donate to help blind girls lead independent lives in society,” urges Shivaprakash.Help Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust break the cycle of neglect. Your donation can give a blind girl her first lesson, her first job, and a life of dignity.Donate to this fundraiser by Give, India’s most trusted online donation platform, to support Divya Jyothi Charitable Trust in its mission to shelter and educate neglected and abandoned blind girls.

campaigns.title: Help 54 Children attain strong Early Education in Pre Primary Classrooms
campaigns.description: Meet Bala. He is 6 years old and studies in Class 1. His father is a driver, and his mother is a daily wage worker.Bala spent two years in pre-primary (LKG and UKG/Anganwadi), yet today he cannot pick out 5 stones from a group of stones, and he finds it hard to listen attentively to classroom instructions in Class 1 now. This is not a lack of ability. Bala did not get a stimulating learning experience before the age of 6.There are many children like Bala. Without quality learning experience in these early years, they enter Class 1 and 2 already behind, and the gap keeps growing.What we are doing about itInidhu Education Foundation runs the Foundational Stage Strengthening Program (FSSP) in 2 government schools in Thiruvarur, Tamil Nadu, reaching 54 pre-primary children. Through play and activity-based learning, we help children build the listening, counting, socio-emotional, and concentration skills they need before they move ahead. Our teachers are implementing well-designed thematic lesson plans with children and providing a holistic learning experience every day.The program runs for 10 months (July 2026 to April 2027). We now need support for the remaining 7 months (October 2026 to April 2027) to cover workbooks, stationery, nutrition and teacher salaries so that the children's progress does not stop midway.Where your money goesWorkbooks - 54 children × ₹500= ₹27,000Story books - 50 books = ₹5000Stationery - 2 schools X ₹700 X 7 months = ₹9800Nutrition- 54 children × ₹5 × 105 days= ₹28,350Teacher salary - 2 teachers × ₹15,000 × 7 months= ₹2,10,000Admin cost - 15000Total program cost is ₹2,80,150That is about ₹5,188 per child for the remaining seven months.How you can helpEvery contribution, big or small, brings a child closer to a strong start. ₹15,000 gives one teacher's salary for a month. ₹5,000 gives one child's education. ₹500 gives one child a workbook.Together, we can make sure children like Bala walk into their learning journey with confidence, curiosity and joy.Please donate and share this with someone who cares about children's education.Our website: https://www.inidhueducation.com/LinkedIn page: https://www.linkedin.com/company/inidhu-education-foundation/

campaigns.title: Therapeutic Community For Victims of Sex Trafficking
campaigns.description:
Commercial sexual exploitation (CSE) is one of the most disparaging crimes crippling India’s social development and economy and threatening the dignity and security of women and children. In this context, the southern states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are no exception. These states continue to constitute the core destination areas for the victimization of trafficked women and children for economic profiteering at the cost of their human rights. Despite the absence of official statistics on CSE in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, civil society organisation estimates suggest that one out of every four victims rescued from CSE is a child and 60 per cent of all rescued children from CSE are HIV positive. Further, 75 per cent of females in the Telugu region between the ages of 15-35 years are found to be engaged in sex work.[1] Reports in the print and digital news media also indicate that sex trafficking of both vulnerable women and children is progressively on the increase. Given the scale of the issue, the government has not placed due attention and priority on the rescue and rehabilitation of CSE victims in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. In addition, there is a lack of systems and capacity to conduct MEL and research, weak and uncoordinated monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) of existing programs and no investment in empirical research to understand gaps and issues. Rehabilitation of trafficking survivors remains the most persistent challenge within the current legislative framework. Rescued victims require specialised support services to recover from and overcome the years of trauma-induced mental health issues, physical atrocities and social stigma attached to being former sex slaves. In the absence of statutory rehabilitation that ensures complete and sustainable reintegration into society, CSE victims, even if removed temporarily from their immediate environment marked by social, economic, sexual, psychological and physical extremities, are highly likely to end up in the same vicious cycle of sex trafficking, either through the nexus of same perpetrators or new agents who are on the lookout for feeding on their aggravated vulnerabilities for the second time around. On-ground organisations lament that CSE victims who only receive piece-meal assistance and support post-rescue remain uncertain about their future prospects in absence of hope for alternate opportunities to sustain themselves and end up going back to sex slavery. The circumstances surrounding this lack of choice with CSE victims are marked by haplessness and isolation due to lack of specialised support services for destigmatizing their identities and acute availability of comprehensive rehabilitation measures. Given the scale of CSE in both Telugu states, the following issues have emerged:There is no comprehensive protection and rehabilitation policy in place for CSE victims, either in the states or at the national level. Nor there are adequate budgetary allocations in the two states. In fact, Andhra Pradesh does not even have a budget line for CSE rehabilitation facilities and services.  Rescue operations for removing victims of CSE from situations of abuse are ill-conceived and ill-executed due to a lack of comprehensive understanding of the crime and tactical expertise and a lack of industry standards for conducting such raids and rescues.Institutional infrastructure (shelter homes/protective and rehabilitative homes/child care institutions) for rehabilitation and reintegration of victims of CSE is insufficient and severely ill-equipped to address their complex needs for recovery and effective, holistic rehabilitation, whose numbers are advancing with each passing year. As per an article published in the Indian Journal of Gender Studies, there is a lack of comprehensive protection services such as psychological counselling from trained counsellors through the Ujjawala and Swadhar schemes. This issue was further exacerbated in 2014 after the bifurcation of the Telugu region between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana 2014, where most rehabilitation homes fell under Telangana’s territory and Andhra Pradesh was left with close to none. At present, both states have 5 shelter homes each, for women.There is a severe gap in meaningful and relevant data to even gain an understanding of the gaps and barriers in the rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of CSE victims. A study suggests that though there is abundant literature on trafficking worldwide as well as in South Asia, we still do need region-specific and locally-contextualised data that will yield theoretical and empirical insights, and lead to relevant policy interventions. 
 Sex trafficking is a multi-dimensional problem especially with regard to its impact on the lives of the victims. The tormenting experiences of being betrayed, sold and exploited by the people around (largely includes pimps, brothel owners and customers) takes a long-term toll on the victims. This traumatic situation combined with sexually transmitted diseases, chronic depression, suicidal tendencies, alcohol and drug addiction complicates the cycle of rehabilitation. Hence, the process of rehabilitation has to be an interlinked chain of psychological healing, vocational empowerment, economically viable and socially acceptable. In order to address the physical, emotional and psychological brokenness of the sex-trafficked victims, Prajwala formulated a holistic, therapeutic approach to support the rehabilitation process. The overall aim is to help the victims to overcome their trauma by providing them with psychological and coping skills and tools required to regain stability to lead a normal life. Therefore, the rehabilitation in Prajwala is a blend of psychological healing, civic empowerment and social identity. The three-pronged stages of rehabilitation spearheaded by Prajwala include:Psychological Rehabilitation: Trauma Care, Counselling, Psychiatric CareEconomic Rehabilitation: Life-Skills, Employability Training, Education/Livelihood programCivic Rehabilitation: Aadhar Card, Bank Account, Interim Relief, CompensationA therapeutic community as a safe shelter has been established that provides holistic rehabilitation and has been instrumental in the social reintegration support of thousands of victims 
 600 victims of sex trafficking will be supported every year

campaigns.title: Prevention and Protection of Tribal Youth from Trafficking
campaigns.description:
The current status and future of tribal children and youth, especially from remote villages of Jharkhand, is pathetic and holds no hope. Lack of access and poor quality education denies children and youth from acquiring reasonable academic qualifications. There are no opportunities for livelihood in their villages, neither are they qualified for the few available jobs in nearby towns and cities. To meet basic needs is a struggle. To add to this dilemma, Tribal communities are constantly losing their land to industries. Their income from farming has taken a nose dive.Human trafficking, particularly that of underage tribal girls shipped out to work as domestic helps in big cities has been a consequence. Recent reports indicate a more heinous level of exploitation where these trafficked girls, are impregnated and made to bear children so that these babies could be sold off. Lack of basic education, traditional beliefs/practices and the girls having no say in the matter contributes to this. Families are driven to a life of resignation, struggling for survival. In this scenario, when an outside agent walks in offering a job and money for their daughter and sons in a far away, unknown world, they are gullible and fall for it. 
 This project will address the root causes of poverty leading to trafficking and abuse of hapless children/youth. The project seeks to provide education from a holistic perspective to bring them out of this complicated web of poverty and misery to transform their lives with hope for a decent and dignified future. The project will have a 3 pronged approach. 1.	Children up to the age of 14 will receive relevant and quality primary education in local government schools according to the provisions of the Right To Education Act.2.	Children/youth in the 15 to 20 age group will be provided with skills training to process non-timber forest products and other agricultural products to enhance their value. Their entrepreneurial skills will be unleashed and they will use online marketing channels to earn a decent living.3.	The Tribal communities will be mobilized and their awareness raised to see the value of their children and protect them from Outside trafficking agents. The communities will demand support from authorities to put an end to trafficking. The project will cover 20 tribal villages and will directly benefit 2,500 children/youth over a 3 year period as well as many others in the years to come. 
 Direct linkages will be established between service providers and the community groups, such that these linkages will continue even after the project period is over. The community will also be involved in advocacy and mobilizing resources. Some of the measurable Results after the 3 year project period will be:•	School enrollment rate and participation rate will be above 95% (up from the present 60%) with quality Learning•	The community will be able to provide relevant, livelihood skills to youth to add value and market locally available materials.•	The established children and youth clubs will continue to function even after the project is over•	The understanding and practice of child rights, especially child participation, will continue •	Trafficking and abuse of children/youth will be challenged by the community and greatly reduce with support from the duty bearers. This awareness and control will spread to the neighbouring villages.•	The SHGs, CLAs and Community Watch Groups will continue their activities.The capacity of the community groups, especially the Community Watch Groups will be strengthened during the 3 year project period in such a way that they can continue to approach duty bearers and claim their entitlements.

campaigns.title: Donate a brick to build a health care clinic for the underprivileged children
campaigns.description:
Help us build a health care clinic for the underprivileged children, in a free school which is located 15 Kms away from the Mysore city.Kaliyuva Mane is a free, child-centric alternative school for the opportunity-deprived children. We have bent every rule that a regular school follows to suit the needs of the children. Approximately 100 Opportunity-deprived children - Child labourers, School Dropouts, Children from BPL families’ etc.., study in our school. The school is located on the outskirts of Mysore, which is 15 Km away from the city. Since we are away from the city, we have to go to Mysore, whenever there is a medical and hospitalization need for children. Also the children who have infections and minor diseases are not isolated from the rest of children, due to the lack of infrastructure. Hence we wanted to build a health care clinic in the school premises itself and hire a full-time nurse, to solve this problem.The total cost of the project is Rs 7.5 Lakhs and our aim is to raise Rs 5 Lakhs (Approx. $ 7,700) for the construction of the health care clinic through this campaign. Assuming a minimum donation of Rs 500, we require 1000 donors (1000 bricks) for this construction.Hence please donate as many bricks as possible for the construction. With the completion of the project, a total of 100 children can avail the medical facilities in the school premises itself.What is the issue addressed in Kaliyuva ManeAccording to a UNESCO report, India has the largest number of adolescent 'out of school' children. As per Annual Status of Education Report, only 42% of rural 5th standard children can read a 2nd standard textbook in their mother tongue.Due to the lack of a proper learning environment at school and home, and because of a turbulent childhood during their formative years, many mentally sound children are deprived of an opportunity to study at regular schools. Rural underprivileged children, child labourers and school dropouts, dyslexic children, children who are unable to adjust to regular schools etc., form this group of opportunity deprived children. 
 Opportunity-deprived children are accompanied with an academic lag or inability to adjust to the strict regimen of a regular school and hence a child-centric alternative school is the need of the hour.Kaliyuva Mane's model of education:• Admissions round the year, as a dropped-out child might regain interest at any point in time• Abolition of grades- Flexible children teams based on knowledge, age and emotional housing of the child• Congenial environment with due importance given to emotions. A happy mind will learn faster.• Individualistic curriculum, taking into consideration the previous academic lag and capability to learn• Evaluation: Regular informal tests rather than annual exams, as initially; memory-testing long duration exams will only instill fear.• 10th Standard: After individualistic training and when the child displays an ability to understand the 10th Std syllabus, the child attempts 10th standard public examination as a private candidate from a formal school. 
 Kaliyuva Mane was started in June 2005 with 14 children, out of which 4 were resident children.• Since 2010, 47 children have appeared for 10th Standard examination in English medium, while 45 have cleared.• 16 children have passed the coveted 10th standard examination, scoring more than 60% marks.• Out of 6 dyslexic children who appeared for the examination, 3 have cleared the 10th standard. The rest could clear all the subjects except one.• Every year, approximately 100 children complete their education at Kaliyuva Mane.• Alumni of this school have already secured gainful employment. Following are the post-matriculation educational courses they have completed/studying: B.E., Diploma in Engineering, B.Sc., B.C.A., B.B.M./B.B.A., B.Com., B.A., PUC (Commerce), ITI, other vocational courses like nursing. We support the post-matriculation education of deserving and needy children.

campaigns.title: Change The Story - Fight The Education Gap
campaigns.description:
In India, there is a significant gap between the rich and poor.- 9 out of 10 students who study in government schools drop out before the 10th grade.- Most of the students are first generation learners whose first language is a local language.- 52% of 5th grade students cannot read 2nd grade text books.- 56% of 8th grade students cannot do simple division.These students tend to not have good role models in their homes or at school. 
 U&I Teach is an after-school program that aims to educate the less privileged youth and help them stay in school. We provide individual attention to students with a 1:3 teacher to student ratio. We provide tuition classes to our students which helps them to excel at difficult subjects like math and science.We also aim to reach out to the students who have already dropped out of school and have no basic education. We want to make sure that these kids have the opportunity to learn as well.Our Teach program provides 360-degree care which includes career days, life skills training, access to a library of books, field trips, medical camps and even counselling. 
 Through our programs, we have created the following changes;- 100% Student pass- 80% of 10th grade students score above 70%- Child's overall developement is better through counselling and medical camps.- Students have good role models to look up to.
